scope: Viewed every PNG listed; read catalog instructions and generation records. Visual/model review, not professional trainer review.

results.reason: Three meaningfully distinct poses show arms down, bilateral front raise and bilateral lateral raise; camera, feet, dumbbells and original branding consistent. No missing unique mechanical transition. Return uses same arms-down pose.
results.necessaryFix: Presentation must follow 01→02→01→03→01 rather than implying front-to-side motion while elevated. This is ordering/reuse, not a need for duplicate PNG.

results.reason: Start plus each distinct overhead arm shown, opposite hand remains at shoulder. Continuous taut cables attach to same low pulleys; active-side stack visibly separates, opposite stays down. No obvious change in selected plate count found, though stack travel/gap differs between sides and minor markings drift. Both hands and full equipment readable.
results.necessaryFix: Present 01→02→01→03→01 and retain same selected load. Do not add a redundant midpress pose solely to inflate phase count.
results.limitations: Rendered stack travel differs side-to-side; this is visual inconsistency worth improving if precise mechanical animation is needed, not a missing phase.

results.reason: Top position and both opposite lowered-arm positions are distinguishable; no unique return pose missing. But near-side lowered kettlebell is drawn very close over nose/face rather than clearly above outside chest, and far-side elbow-floor contact is occluded by torso, so exact safe bottom geometry is not demonstrable from this view.
results.necessaryFix: Correct lowered-arm images using a slightly more elevated frontal footward view across entire sequence if necessary: elbow visibly touches floor 30–45° from torso, forearm vertical, wrist directly above elbow, bell clearly outside chest and away from face. Keep opposite weight extended. Retain 01→02→01→03→01.

results.reason: Five images include distinct takeoff-ready, flight, landing, opposite flight, opposite landing, so quantity is enough. However ready foreground right foot is advanced, then same near-side right knee appears raised rather than opposite knee; opposite pair turns torso/head facing the other direction and behaves like a mirrored first pair. Horizontal line and repeated contact depth do not establish forward-diagonal travel. Shirt branding shifts/lettering drifts.
results.necessaryFix: Regenerate same fixed front-facing camera with constant torso orientation, explicit right-foot push→left-knee flight→left-foot landing→left-foot push→right-knee flight→right-foot landing. Use fixed floor depth cues and two diagonal landing locations to make trajectory readable; a subtle yellow directional arrow can help. Do not accept current draft.

results.reason: Full working repetition is visually readable: upright start→mid-descent→bottom→upright return. Same bar load, camera, foot contacts and elbow-crook support broadly consistent, no obvious missing unique phase. Yellow descent/ascent arrows clarify direction. No reason to regenerate merely to add a redundant return intermediate.
results.necessaryFix: Create absent generation record/provenance if recoverable; independently verify controversial catalog cues about knees not passing toes and rising predominantly through forefoot before treating text as validated trainer guidance.
results.limitations: No trainer review; three-quarter angle partly hides far elbow contact. Record was absent.
